validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of vitamin E literature whose only original data are in vitro tests on a human prostate cancer cell line, with no human incidence analysis.

validated_results.title: Alcohol and prostate cancer in the NHANES I epidemiologic follow-up study. First National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey of the United States.
validated_results.reason: Original prospective cohort analysis of alcohol consumption and incident prostate cancer in NHANES I follow-up reporting relative risks.

extraction.comparison_type: heaviest level of drinking versus lower usual total alcohol consumption
extraction.population: Men aged 25-74 years in the NHANES I Epidemiologic Follow-up Study

sample_size.excerpt: There were two cohorts: 1) Cohort I, followed from baseline (1971-75) through 1992, included 5766 men ages 25-74 years (median follow-up = 17 years); and 2) Cohort II, followed from the first follow-up round for Cohort I (1982-84) through 1992, included the 3868 men in Cohort I free of prostate cancer in 1982-84 (median follow-up = 9 years).

cases.excerpt: There were 252 incident cases of prostate cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Consistent with most previous studies, we found no significant associations between usual total alcohol consumption and prostate cancer in Cohorts I or II [p = non significant (NS)], except for a significant inverse association at the heaviest level of drinking in Cohort II [relative risk (RR) = 0.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.06-0.95].

confidence_interval.excerpt: Consistent with most previous studies, we found no significant associations between usual total alcohol consumption and prostate cancer in Cohorts I or II [p = non significant (NS)], except for a significant inverse association at the heaviest level of drinking in Cohort II [relative risk (RR) = 0.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.06-0.95].

design.excerpt: We prospectively investigated the association between alcohol consumption and prostate cancer in the Epidemiologic Follow-up Study (NHEFS)

timing.excerpt: Alcohol consumption was assessed at baseline as usual consumption, and at follow-up as usual consumption and as distant past consumption

continent.excerpt: First National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey of the United States

location.excerpt: First National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey of the United States

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Alcohol consumption was assessed at baseline as usual consumption
